note: Visible appearance only (Addendum 01 §13, Addendum 02 §9.1). Nothing here is a simulation input: mechanical parts live in parts.json. Wheel fitment keeps the tyre outer radius at the chassis value (the sidewall absorbs a rim size change) and offsets stay inside the measured arch clearance, so no choice clips a tyre or changes grip, gearing, ride height or track.

conventions.anchors: Normalised to the body bounding box: x -0.5..0.5 of width (+ right), y 0..1 of height (0 = ground), z -0.5..0.5 of length (+ forward). mount names the surface the part attaches to.
conventions.decalZones: u, v in 0..1 across the painted panel of a zone, in the renderer frame (CarBodyGenerator surface). left/right flanks: u = 0 at the rear, 1 at the front; v = 0 at the sill, 1 at the waist. hood: u from the car's left to right, v = 0 at the windscreen, 1 at the nose. roof: u left to right, v = 0 at the rear. front: u from the car's left to right; rear: u from the car's right to left; v bottom to top. keepOut rectangles (lamps, plates, intakes) are masked so decals can never hide lamps or the plate. Decal scale is the size on the body in metres (0.05..1.6).
conventions.decalRender: render is the procedural kind the renderer draws (stripe, twin-stripe, pinstripe, circle, ring, arrow, chevron, star, bars, arcs, flame, hex, digit, text); digit and text carry a glyph. Decal text is authored only - players never type decal text. Cosmetic mapping: COS-CH01 Tea-Line Pinstripe -> pinstripe; COS-CH02 Brake Marker Bars -> bars; COS-CH03 Orchard Apex Arcs -> arcs; COS-CH04 Rising Tea Arrow -> arrow; COS-CH05 Bellmaker Thread -> pinstripe; COS-CH06 Cedar Chevron -> chevron; COS-CH07 Release Trace -> stripe; COS-CH08 Rain Window -> bars; COS-CH09 Viaduct Twin Lines -> twin-stripe; COS-CH10 Reservoir Twinmark -> ring; COS-CH11 Blackwater Needle -> arrow; COS-CH12 Quarry Last Marker -> hex; COS-CH13 Moonridge Edgework -> arcs; COS-CH14 Datum Continuum -> stripe; COS-CH15 Amanagi Dawnseal -> star.
conventions.wheels: diameterIn is the rim diameter in whole inches (one step = 1 in); the tyre outer radius stays tyreRadiusM. offsetStep moves the wheel face 5 mm per step (+ outward); outward steps are limited by archClearanceMm with a 5 mm margin.

notes.exhaust: Narrow rear bumper (1.63 m): quad tips would crowd the plate recess, so dual and center are the visible tip options.

notes.rearAero: Three-door hatch: there is no trunk deck for a ducktail or a pedestal GT wing, so the rear-aero family is the documented hatch equivalent - lip-spoiler (hatch-glass lip) and wing (roof-edge spoiler).

Narrow rear bumper (1.70 m): quad tips would crowd the plate recess, so dual and center are the visible tip options.

notes.rearAero: Light roadster: a raised wing would sit in the folding roof's path and misread the car, so the documented equivalent is deck-integrated - ducktail and lip-spoiler on the long open rear deck.
notes.exhaust: Narrow rear bumper (1.68 m): quad tips would crowd the plate recess, so dual and center are the visible tip options.
notes.paint: Roadster: the roof zone is the removable hardtop; its two-tone and decals show whenever the hardtop is fitted.

notes.rearAero: Hot hatch: no trunk deck for a ducktail, so lip-spoiler (hatch-glass lip) is the documented equivalent; wing and gt-wing mount on the roof edge like time-attack hatches.
notes.exhaust: Narrow rear bumper (1.75 m): quad tips would crowd the plate recess, so dual and center are the visible tip options.

notes.rearAero: Touring wagon: the long cargo roof and vertical tailgate leave no deck for a ducktail or GT wing; the documented equivalent is lip-spoiler (tailgate lip) and wing (roof-edge spoiler behind the rails).
notes.exhaust: Narrow rear bumper (1.73 m): quad tips would crowd the plate recess, so dual and center are the visible tip options.

card.note: Player Card style (spec §11): free defaults for everyone; the fifteen card_customization challenge rewards (COS-CH46 to COS-CH60) and the seven accessory_or_avatar avatars are locked until owned. Visual only.

wardrobe.note: The driver's reward wardrobe (spec §11 appearance; challenge rewards: clothing and accessories render on the driver's avatar). Fifteen driver_clothing garments (COS-CH31 to COS-CH45) and the eight worn accessory_or_avatar rewards; the other seven accessory_or_avatar rewards are card avatars. Each item is locked until owned; a garment replaces that part of the player's own outfit while worn. Visual only.
